headline: vCenter zero-day, PHP firewall exploits, and four new KEV entries
standfirst: Virtualization and the network edge dominate: a vCenter authentication bypass was exploited before a patch, PHP flaws reached firewall management interfaces, and CISA added four exploited vulnerabilities. Breach disclosures and an encryption notice round out the day.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

A critical VMware vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day by a China-linked espionage group before Broadcom released a patch [[s1]]. Analysis: the significance is placement. vCenter is the control plane for virtualization estates, so an authentication bypass there can expose management rather than a single workload. The supplied excerpt does not name the CVE, affected vCenter versions, or the exploitation window; those details are not available here.

Attackers exploited two PHP flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, with a firewall among the early PHP2Shell targets [[s27]]. Both CVEs are in CISA KEV, both are rated CVSS 4.0 9.2 Critical, and both can lead to remote code execution in PHP. Their vectors show network access, no privileges and no user interaction, but high attack complexity. NVD also lists PAN-OS 10.2.0 before 10.2.7 in the affected configurations, so the supplied exposure set extends beyond PHP itself. CISA’s required action is to apply mitigations per vendor instructions.

CISA added four vulnerabilities to KEV on evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2024-10441 in Synology DSM (9.8 Critical), CVE-2026-40217 in LiteLLM (8.8 High), CVE-2026-90436 in Apache Axis (9.8 Critical) and CVE-2026-90817 in REDCap (9.8 Critical) [[s45]]. The set is not uniformly critical: LiteLLM’s vector requires low privileges; Axis is unauthenticated; REDCap is unauthenticated but requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash. Axis 1.x is end-of-life through 1.4, and the supplied description says migrating or using a patched build are the options. Analysis: the spread — NAS management, LiteLLM, a legacy SOAP engine and research data capture — illustrates how KEV risk can sit in internet-reachable middleware rather than headline platforms.

Cisco Expressway exploitation came soon after a public proof of concept: attackers compromised clustered Expressway devices at a Russian organization and prepared tooling for lateral movement [[s19]]. The excerpt does not name the CVE, the affected versions, or confirm internet exposure. Analysis: the case fits the pattern of edge appliances moving from PoC to intrusion quickly, though a single incident cannot establish a general tempo.

## Breaches

The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack in which intruders used ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform that the FBI had warned was being used by criminals and state-sponsored groups [[s11]]. The confirmed element is tooling use; the excerpt does not establish the actor, the intrusion vector, or whether ARTEX was decisive.

Transport for London said around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had account details exposed [[s3]]. “May have” is doing real work: the supplied wording describes a possible exposure, not a confirmed count of exfiltrated records.

## Vulnerabilities

F5 patched five critical NGINX2Root vulnerabilities that could allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code, with public proof-of-concept exploits raising the stakes [[s31]]. The excerpt does not supply CVE IDs or affected NGINX versions; those details are not available here.

## Industry

A UK tribunal confirmed the government served Apple with a secret legal notice targeting cryptographic protections for iCloud accounts, ending almost two years of official refusal to acknowledge it [[s8]]. The excerpt does not supply the notice’s technical scope, legal basis, or operational effect.

nvd.description: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

nvd.description: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

nvd.description:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation. When a SOAP <Fault> carries a <detail><exceptionName> element, Axis loads the named class and, if a String <data> element is also present, instantiates it through its String constructor before checking that it is an AxisFault. Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's classpath this leads to remote code execution. The fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it. This affects all Apache Axis 1.x versions through 1.4.



As Axis 1 has been EOL we recommend you migrate to a different SOAP engine, such as Apache Axis 2/Java. Alternatively you could use a build of Axis with the patch from https://github.com/apache/axis-axis1-java/commit/41f3b4e8d04e310ca81f86b92630ab2c11d608bd applied. The Apache Axis project does not expect to create an Axis 1.x release fixing this problem.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) contains a code injection vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server. An attacker could exploit this via crafted HTTP requests that access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and supply a crafted file-path or stream parameter during data import processing. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash.

nvd.description: An unauthenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerability was found in the survey passthrough routing and Data Import processing logic, in which a malicious user could potentially exploit it by manipulating HTTP requests to access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and by supplying a crafted file-path/stream parameter during import handling. If successfully exploited, this could allow the attacker to remotely execute arbitrary code on the REDCap server. The attacker does not have to be authenticated in order to exploit this, but exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash. This vulnerability exists in REDCap 13.3.0 and higher.

alsoCollected.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
alsoCollected.excerpt: PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server. Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 and rated

nvd.description:
Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

nvd.description:
Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.



Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service.



This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.
